description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives (PDO) are (i) to increase access to and quality of water supply services, (ii) to increase access to sanitation, and (iii) to improve the operational performance of the water supply services provider(s) and water resources management in Greater Lome.

Togo has abundant water resources, but their management in Greater Lome faces significant challenges, including vulnerability to climate change. Just half of the Togolese population has access to water supply services and only 16 percent to improved sanitation, among the lowest coverage levels in the region. The expansion of production capacity in Lome, necessary to the improvement of service coverage and quality, will require the development of large, capital intensive surface water development schemes. The water sector institutional framework has been reformed in 2014, but sector efficiency remains low and further improvements are still needed, in particular on regulation. The long-term sector financial viability is not guaranteed, due to a combination of low operational efficiency and insufficient tariff contribution to sector deficit.The proposed Project will focus on improving water and sanitation services, strengthening the water and sewerage services provider TdE (Togolaise des Eaux) to improve the sustainability of services and improving water resources management. The project will benefit a total of 950,000 people in Greater Lome. The entire population of the capital city currently connected to TdE water supply system, more than 750,000 people, is expected to benefit from improved quality of water supply services, in terms of service pressure and continuity. In addition, it is expected that 200,000 people in Greater Lome (more than half of which are women) will be connected to TdE water supply systems under the Project, gaining access to improved, climate-resilient water supply services. Finally, 110 schools and medical centers will gain access to water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. The proposed Project will have five components as follows:Component 1 will aim to improve access to safe water supply services in the Greater Lome and finance (i) the construction and rehabilitation of water production and treatment systems; (ii) the construction and rehabilitation of water storage facilities; (iii) the rehabilitation, replacement and expansion of water supply transmission and distribution systems; and (iv) supervision consultancies. It will include the creation of six autonomous water supply systems in the peripheral areas of Sanguera, Apessito, Kohe, Adeticope Est, Devego and Togblekope. Expansion of water production capacity is expected to be achieved from groundwater sources, through the construction of new boreholes and rehabilitation of existing ones.Component 2 is designed to contribute to the sustainability of water-related investments funded under Component 1 and will help improve the operational efficiency and financial viability of Togolaise des Eaux (TdE), the national water utility. The activities will include the mobilization of a technical assistance to help TdE reduce non-revenue water and improve customer management while strengthening its operational capacity. The component will also support the provision of studies and technical assistance to improve sector governance and assets management.Component 3 will support the construction and/or rehabilitation of WASH facilities in schools and Health Care Centers, including water taps connected to TdE network, gender-disaggregated latrines with septic tanks, handwashing stations, menstrual health hygiene (MHH) facilities, etc. The component will foresee the organization of awareness campaigns and the development of O&M plans to finance and maintain WASH services. The component will also support the formulation of a fecal sludge management strategy.Component 4 will aim to improve the understanding and management of water resources in Greater Lome. The activities include (i) the implementation of hydrological studies of Greater Lome's coastal sedimentary aquifers to inform groundwater abstraction development and sustainable management plans; (ii) the identification of aquifer contamination risks around TdE boreholes and mitigation measures, (iii) development of water use and surface water and groundwater resources geographic information system, database and data collection system; (iv) implementation and rehabilitation of hydrological and piezometric monitoring stations; (v) training of Ministry of Water and Sanitation and other relevant authorities to collect, analyze, and publish water resource information. Component 5: Project management, sector studies and supervision will support MEA in project management. This will include, but not limited to, the operating cost of the PMU, project implementation technical assistance, and consultants that will support the design of sub-projects and sector studies.The proposed Project is aligned with the World Bank's twin goals of ending extreme poverty and promoting shared prosperity. Under the World Bank's Systematic Country Diagnostic (SCD) 2022, High Level Objective 5 focuses on “increased resilience of poor and vulnerable to shocks and sustainability of natural capital”, with “access to water and sanitation” identified as one of the key action areas to achieve it. Many of the recommended priority actions (improving TdE's operational capacity, strengthening the regulatory agency, improve knowledge of water resources in Lome) are directly supported under the proposed project. The first consultations for the preparation of the Country Partnership Framework (CPF) 2023-2027 have reconfirmed the importance of water security, in particular as a key contributor to food security.

condition.narrative: Per ESCP: Adopt and publish the ESMF prior to Project appraisal and thereafter implement the ESMF throughout Projectimplementation. The Resettlement Policy Framework is adopted and published prior to Board approval. The Labor Management Plan isdeveloped, validated and published prior to Board approval. The Stakeholders Engagement Plan is adopted and published prior toBoard approval and updated no later than one year after the Effective Date of the Project. The implementation of these plans andtheir actions are carried out throughout the implementation of the Project. Sub-project specific ESIA/ESMP shall be adopted andpublished and validated by the PMU, the Association and national agencies prior to issuing the tender documents. They must then beimplemented throughout the implementation of the Project.
Per ESCP: Establish the grievance mechanism prior to the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain and operate the mechanismthroughout Project implementation.

Per ESCP: Training on ESS no later than 3 months after Project Effective Date. During the recruitment of PMU ES specialists andrepeated once a year throughout the implementation of the Project. Training on OHS before the start of employment of newlyrecruited workers or activities for existing employers. Training will be provided every 6 months throughout the implementation ofthe Project. Training on employment and working conditions before the start of employment of newly recruited workers or activitiesfor existing employees. Training will be provided every 6 months throughout the implementation of the Project. Environmental andsocial management training, training on the Grievance Redress Mechanism and training on SEA/SH/VAC risk no later than 3 monthsafter Project Effective Date.

Schedule 2, section I.A.(b) i. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall maintain, at all times during the implementation ofthe Project, the Project Implementation Unit (“PIU”), with terms of reference, qualified staffing and resources satisfactory totheAssociation, to be responsible for overall coordination as well as day-to-day management, supervision and administration of theProject activities and results, fiduciary aspects (financial management and procurement), environmental and social standardsaspects, reporting and communication of Project activities, and monitoring and evaluation of Project activities, all inaccordance with the provisions of the Project Implementation Manual.

Schedule 2, section I.A.(b) ii. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall, no later than three (3) months after the EffectiveDate, or any later date agreed by the Association, recruit or appoint an accountant for the PIU, with experience and under terms ofreference satisfactory to the Association

Schedule 2, section I.A.(b) iv. of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall establish and maintain at all times during theimplementation of the Project a Project Steering Committee, which shall for the purposes of facilitating inter agency-coordination,all under terms of reference, composition, and powers acceptable to the Association and further described in the ImplementationManual.

Schedule 2, section I.B.1 of the Financing Agreement. The Recipient shall prepare under terms of reference acceptable to theAssociation, and no later than three (3) months after the effective date furnish the Association, an implementation manual for theProject containing detailed arrangements and procedures for: (a) institutional coordination and day-to-day execution of theProject; (b) Project budgeting, disbursement and financial management; (c) procurement; (d) monitoring, evaluation, reporting andcommunication; (e) safeguards monitoring and mitigation; (f) operational modules outlining implementation, organizational,administrative, monitoring, financial management, disbursement procurement, and (g) such other arrangements and procedures as shallbe required for the Project (“Project Implementation Manual” or “PIM”).
